newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Celsius back to profit despite defence cuts.
newsitem.headline: Celsius back to profit despite defence cuts.

text.p: Swedish defence group Celsius AB said on Thursday that despite cutbacks in defence spending in Sweden and overseas it managed to return to the black in 1996.
Celsius posted a profit after financial items of 347 million crowns ($46.5 million) against a loss of 559 million crowns in 1995 as foreshadowed in preliminary figures released in early February.

However the loss in 1995 was due to heavy restructuring costs in two of its five business units. Arms manufacturing unit Bofors and submarine group Kockums were scaled down with 1,200 jobs axed in line with defence force cuts.

"As a consequence of uncertainty concerning the scope of Sweden's future defence-material requirement, most Celsius group business areas have reported a weak inflow of orders from the Swedish defence forces," Celsius' chief executive Olle Lund said in a statement.
"Nevertheless an increasing share of civil-sector orders, combined with some export successes in the defence sector, has compensated for this decline."
Celsius said operating income in 1996 accounted for 99 million crowns of net income for the year while the net of financial items added a further 248 million crowns.
"Due to successful treasury operations during 1996 we have achieved a very good return on our financial assets," Lund said.
"Towards the end of the year we also noted a rise in operating income. The good results generated by the maintenance operations were especially encouraging."
The company reported sales in 1996 rose to 11.11 billion crowns from 10.82 billion crowns.
Despite cutbacks in defence allocations in Sweden and internationally there was a 15 percent increase in the number of order received during the year to 10.46 billion crowns.
Celsius, whose other units are FFV Aerotech, CelsiusTech and Celsius Invest, proposed a 1996 dividend payment of 3.40 crowns a share. It did not pay a dividend in 1995.
